I've been farming these 4.5 mu for 35 years, and with my university education I read the county agricultural bulletins and talk with the agro-input dealer in town. But I'll be honest — on a small plot like mine, I stick close to what worked last year and what the neighbors do, because one bad harvest hurts more than wasting a bit of fertilizer.

My rotation is winter wheat then summer maize, same as everyone around Quzhou. I have well irrigation, which is good because spring here is dry.

For winter wheat, I plant an improved variety — Jimai 22 did well for me last three years, so I'll buy that again, about 15 kg seed per mu because our soil is decent. I apply compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as base, roughly 50 kg per mu before plowing, which gives me about 7.5 kg each of N, P, K. Then I topdress urea twice — once at greening (spring), maybe 15 kg urea per mu, and again at jointing, another 15 kg. That puts my total N around 21 kg/mu. I know the extension says 18 is enough, but I'd rather have a bit extra than see yellow leaves. I irrigate 4 times: winter water before freeze, greening, jointing, and grain-filling. Pesticide 2-3 times — aphids and powdery mildew are my main worries. After maize harvest I rotary-till the stubble. I expect around 500 kg/mu; last year I got 510.

For summer maize, I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid, about 2.5 kg seed per mu. I do no-till direct seeding right after wheat harvest — saves me 3-4 days which matters for getting full growing season. Base fertilizer 40 kg compound (15-15-15) at sowing, then topdress 25 kg urea at the big trumpet stage. That's around 24 kg N total. Maize likes nitrogen. Irrigate 2-3 times depending on rain — usually after sowing and at tasseling. Two pesticide sprays for corn borer and armyworm. I expect 600 kg/mu.

My family has 6 people and some work off-farm, so 4.5 mu doesn't feed us — it's supplementary income and our own grain. I don't want to cheap out on inputs because the yield loss would hurt more than the saved cost.
